coverage.courseMaterialOnlyNote: Lecture 11's slide deck is transcribed (all 58 pages) and its 32 figure slides are rendered, but it has no transcript and no wiki page, so it is NOT counted in lecturesCovered. Cite it as course material, and say that the lecture itself is not yet covered.

images.format: For the six PDF decks: whole slides rendered at 1400px, JPEG q85 or PNG whichever is smaller, named by PDF page number. For the four executable lectures: the course's own images/*.png, fetched unmodified from the lectures repo.
images.discovery: inline in wiki/ and raw/slides/; no index file
images.note: Coverage is every figure-bearing page of each deck (46 of 67, 48 of 60, 51 of 55, 51 of 73, 40 of 57, 32 of 58), and the course's own figures for the executable lectures, which have no deck. Roughly a third of each deck was deliberately NOT rendered - title cards, outlines, section dividers, pure-text bullets, and the pasted tables and equation blocks that raw/slides already reproduces cell by cell. So an image path must be read from a file, never constructed: slide-31.jpg existing says nothing about slide-32.jpg. LECTURE 11 IS THE EXCEPTION TO READ CAREFULLY: it has 32 images but no wiki page, so they are reachable only from raw/slides/11-scaling-laws-in-the-wild.md.

license.summary: No single repository-wide licence. Three layers: (1) the compilation's own editorial work - INDEX/AGENTS/SEE_ALSO/TODO/kb.json/sources.md and the original explanatory prose in wiki/ - is CC-BY-4.0; (2) Stanford CS336 course material, including everything in raw/images/ and the content described in raw/slides/, has NO licence of any kind and is included for study under fair use; (3) third-party paper figures reproduced inside the decks belong to their authors. raw/transcripts/ and raw/slides/ are derivative works and are NOT offered under CC BY, because the underlying lecture and slides are not the compiler's to license.

courseMaterial.basis: fair use (17 U.S.C. 107); reliance is the compiler's and does not transfer to a reader
courseMaterial.evidence: stanford-cs336/lectures has no LICENSE/LICENSE.md/COPYING/NOTICE; its README states no reuse terms; cs336.stanford.edu carries no licence, copyright or reuse statement; no page of any transcribed deck contains licence text and no PDF records one in metadata; the YouTube recordings carry no Creative Commons marker, consistent with the default Standard YouTube License.

thirdPartyFigures.note: Reproduced inside the decks with a credit line, and not licensable by Stanford or by this compilation. 32 distinct cited sources across the 236 rendered pages; heaviest is Kaplan et al. at 8 pages over three lectures, then Fedus et al. at 8 in one; only 3 of 32 appear on more than three pages.
thirdPartyFigures.arxivLicensesChecked: 2026-09-03: 9 of the 10 most-reproduced sources are arXiv nonexclusive-distrib/1.0, which grants arXiv distribution rights and third parties none. The exception is Wei et al., Emergent Abilities (arXiv:2206.07682), which is CC BY 4.0.

license.takedown: Open a GitHub issue or contact the repository owner; the file and every reference to it are deleted and the removal noted here.

caveats: PARTIAL: covers lectures 1-10 of 18. Do not cite this KB as covering CS336 as a whole. Lectures 11-18 - advanced scaling laws, evaluation, data, alignment, mid/post-training, RLVR and multimodality - have no transcripts and no wiki pages. Note in particular that CS336 splits scaling laws across two lectures with inference in between: lecture 9 (basics) and lecture 10 (inference) are covered in full, lecture 11 (advanced - muP in depth, modern open-model tech reports, optimizers) is not.

materials.method is 'mixed' and the split matters. Lectures 1, 2, 6, 7 and 10 are executable Python programs (lecture_01.py, lecture_02.py, lecture_06.py, lecture_07.py, lecture_10.py), transcribed exactly from source text; that is not a lower grade than page-images, because there are no slides to have looked at. Lectures 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9 are PDF decks (67, 60, 55, 73 and 57 pages) read as page images, so their figures, charts and tables ARE captured. See materials.byLecture.

Figures: fully described for the five deck lectures (3, 4, 5, 8, 9), where a reader looked at every page. For the five executable lectures (1, 2, 6, 7, 10) raw/slides records each image() call at the point it appears; the 45 figures the course serves from its own repo are committed under raw/images/ and each carries a written description, but the figures those lectures display by EXTERNAL URL (NVIDIA documentation, arXiv, Wikimedia, Springer, the JAX scaling book, Baseten, Anyscale) are recorded as links only, with no description of their contents. No wiki claim rests on one of those. This matters most for lectures 4 and 5, whose decks are 102 images across 60 pages and 83 across 55 with most pages carrying under 40 words of native text - the figure descriptions there carry the content rather than illustrating it.

None of the three transcribed decks prints a page number on any page, so slide labels in raw/slides/03-architectures.md, 04-attention-alternatives.md and 05-gpus-tpus.md are PDF page numbers, and all three files say so in their front matter. For lecture 3 a page-number scan reported one printed number; that glyph is the numerator of the MQA arithmetic-intensity fraction on page 61, not a folio. For lecture 4 the scan reported none and all 60 pages were checked by eye. For lecture 5 the scan reported none, a corner-position text-layer scan returned only mid-page body text, and the three readers who split the deck each confirmed the absence independently over their own range. On lecture 5 the numbering was derived in the parent BEFORE any page was read and handed to the readers as a conclusion, so no reader made a numbering judgement of its own.

Lecture 3's figure descriptions were audited against the PDF at 600-1200 dpi on 8 figure- and table-heavy pages (11, 12, 46, 50, 52, 55, 63, 67). Six were clean and both large numeric tables were exact cell for cell. Three errors were found and fixed: two sparse columns on slide 67 asserted to be uniformly empty (MoE is checked on GPT4 and Mixtral; Parametrization carries MuP on the Phi3 row), and one self-contradiction on slide 55 about whether an annotation was covered. Separately, the four views of the model database on slides 7, 29, 51 and 67 were cross-checked against each other: 296 overlapping cells, zero disagreements.

Lecture 4's figure descriptions were audited against the PDF at 600-2200 dpi on 8 chart- and table-heavy pages (6, 11, 16, 20, 33, 35, 43, 52). Five were clean and 9 corrections were applied across pages 6, 11 and 43. Every one of the 9 was a chart value read slightly off, not a structural error: nothing was fabricated, no series was transposed, and all four audited tables (page 20's Llama 4 screenshot, page 35's 12-row native routing table, page 52's MiniCPM Table 6, page 6's ablation table) were exact cell for cell. The largest error was a systematic ~0.13 offset across one OLMoE validation-loss panel on page 43, from reading a linear x-axis as though it were spaced otherwise. Every claim the transcribers had themselves flagged as uncertain proved correct on audit.

Lecture 4's deck contradicts itself in three places, and the transcription records each as printed rather than reconciling it: slide 47's printed expert-index vector '1 2 0 2 1 2' disagrees with its own stage labels (experts 0 and 2 swapped); slide 56's heading says 'Shared (1)' for DeepSeek v3 while its diagram shows two shared experts, and its bold line reads 'V2 (671B - 37 active)' under a v3 title; slide 39's code screenshot applies a jitter drawn around 1 with '+=' rather than '*='. Separately, slides 16 and 17 both plot Switch-Base runs but use different colour assignments and different series counts, so they must not be cross-quoted by colour, and slide 20's Llama 4 table screenshot is cropped mid-row below GPQA Diamond in the source image.

One value in lecture 4's slide file was NOT read off the page: the FlashAttention-2 bar at 1k sequence length on slide 3, whose label the chart's own legend box overprints. It is recorded as 153 TFLOPs/s on external confirmation from the KB's author, and the entry says so. The visible digits and bar height are consistent with that value.

Worked numeric values in lectures 1 and 2 do not appear in the lecture sources - they are produced at runtime by @inspect annotations. Deterministic arithmetic (FLOP counts, byte counts, arithmetic intensities, memory totals) was recomputed by evaluating the lecture's own expressions verbatim and is marked '(computed)'. Measurements (wall-clock timings, measured FLOP/s, MFU, peak-memory readings) depend on the GPU the program runs on, are marked 'machine-dependent, not reproduced', and are given NO value. Percy states at 17:03 that he ran lecture 2 on a laptop with no GPU, so the values shown in class were not produced on the hardware they describe either.

Transcripts were copy-edited from auto-captions. The verbatim captions are NOT committed to this repo - they are a complete reproduction of each lecture with none of this KB's own work in them - but they stay reproducible on demand from the video id in each transcript's front matter, so any edit here can still be audited against them. The lecture 2, 3 and 4 edits were drafted by claude-sonnet-5 and adjudicated against three mechanical checks (timestamp sequence, number inventory, per-paragraph word ratios). Places where the captions are genuinely ambiguous are marked inline with [Ed:] notes rather than guessed. Lecture 4 retains ~84% of the caption word count against lecture 3's ~90%, because that speaker leans much more heavily on 'you know' / 'sort of' / 'kind of'; the three paragraphs falling outside the expected ratio band were each read against the original and confirmed to be filler removal only.

Lecture 2's transcript carries four [Ed:] notes where what Percy said and what his own program computes disagree - GPT-3's FLOP count, an 8-H100 FLOP total, a matmul arithmetic intensity he self-corrects, and the recomputation cost of sqrt(L) checkpointing. The wiki follows the lecture source in each case and says so.

Lecture 3's transcript carries nine [Ed:] notes, and two are load-bearing for the wiki. At 26:08 the captions garble the sentence naming GPT-3 as an ungated counterexample; the wiki follows the deck, which states it unambiguously. At 30:43 the captions have Falcon described as an exception that 'use[s] a gated linear unit', which contradicts both the word 'exception' and the deck's own table (Falcon 2 11B is GeLU), suggesting a dropped negation. Adjudication also reverted one over-confident restoration: the draft had written 'Nemotron-4 340B' where the captions have 'NeMo Tron 340B', but slide 26 prints 'Nemotron 340B' and the speaker was reading that slide, so the digit was removed.

Lecture 4's transcript carries five [Ed:] notes. One is load-bearing for the wiki: at 1:20:51 Hashimoto says MiniCPM was upcycled to a '13.4 billion parameter' model while slide 52's table prints 'MiniCPM-MoE (13.6B)'. The transcript leaves the spoken figure as spoken and records the disagreement; wiki/upcycling.md cites the deck as the better authority for a printed number. Two further [Ed:] notes mark garbled student questions whose wording could not be recovered.

Lecture 5's figure descriptions were audited against the PDF in TWO passes at 600-2400 dpi, 14 pages in total. Pass 1 covered pages 6, 10, 17, 27, 29, 46, 47 (three clean, nine corrections); a 4-of-7 dirty rate meant the sample was too small, so pass 2 covered pages 9, 14, 20, 21, 33, 48, 55 (five clean, five corrections). Unlike lectures 3 and 4, where audits found chart VALUES read slightly off, every one of the 14 errors here was structural: miscounted overlay arrows (twice, on the two pages showing the same chart), a five-region colour wash called four, an annotation said to have an arrow it does not have, die-edge bars placed on the wrong edges and miscounted, GPC blocks counted as four when there are eight, an NVLink row hedged as 8-10 when there are twelve, a red highlight attributed to the wrong figure, uniformity claims true of one sub-block in four, a data grid in eight colour groups called four, a legend in the wrong corner, and one entire figure on slide 27 that had gone unmentioned. Across all 14 pages, every data series, table cell, bit-field and numeric spot-check matched the source exactly - including pixel-measured elbow positions on the roofline chart and a field-by-field check of two FX-graph diagrams. The corrected slide 9 (eight GPCs) also now agrees with slide 10's own die panel, which prints 'x8 GPC'.

Lecture 5's deck contradicts itself in one place that a reader may hit: slide 27 gives MXFP8's scale factors as FP8 E8M0, one per 32 elements, while slide 29 gives MXFP4 as one per 16 with E4M3 scale factors. The audit confirmed both texts verbatim and confirmed that slide 29 names no other format anywhere on the page, so this is the deck's own inconsistency, not a transcription error; wiki/microscaling-formats.md records both and tells the reader to check a vendor specification for an authoritative encoding. Two further oddities are transcribed as printed rather than corrected: slide 17's x-axis reads 'M80' where the Maxwell part is normally called M40 (confirmed at 2400 dpi), and slide 34's caption calls the stored activations 'yellow' while the diagram renders them orange.

Lecture 5's transcript carries five [Ed:] notes and one adjudication worth knowing about. The Sonnet draft had completed two of the speaker's aborted false starts with words he never said - 'divisible by two' where the captions have 'not even divi-', and 'diminishing returns' where he self-corrects to 'penalties'. Both were reverted and the header now states that false starts are preserved rather than completed. Two restored proper nouns, 'Groq' and 'Chris Re', appear nowhere in the deck and rest partly on knowledge outside the course material; the transcript header labels both as such rather than implying document support.

Lecture 5 quotes two different SM counts for an A100 and both are correct in context: 128 at [10:02], read off slide 10's GA100 die annotation, and 108 on slide 48, which is the shipped product's count and the one the wave-quantization arithmetic depends on. wiki/wave-quantization.md and wiki/gpu-architecture.md both explain the difference rather than silently picking one.

Two numbers in lecture 5's deck are printed oddly and are recorded as printed rather than reconciled: slide 14's H100 column gives 32MB for both the SMEM row and the Registers row, and slide 55's bullets carry the deck's own typos ('Curent', 'doesnt'). Neither is a transcription error; both were confirmed against the rendered page.
Lecture 6 is an executable lecture (lecture_06.py), so it is source-text: its figures are recorded by path only and no wiki claim rests on one, exactly as for lectures 1 and 2.

Lecture 6's benchmark timings and all four of its profiler tables are measurements of the lecturer's own GPU. They are marked machine-dependent and NOT reproduced anywhere in this KB — including the naive/built-in/compiled GeLU comparison, which is stated qualitatively as the lecture states it. Do not quote a number for them.

Lecture 6's own source contradicts itself once: the warp-occupancy example says in prose 'thread block has 64 threads' while the code beneath it sets num_threads_per_block = 128. The KB reports the code's values (occupancy 0.1875) and flags the discrepancy in both raw/slides and wiki/warp-occupancy.md.
The Cairn catalog titles lecture 6 'Kernels, Triton, XLA', but XLA and JAX appear nowhere in either the lecture source or the captions. This KB uses the course site's name, 'Kernels, Triton'.

One name in lecture 6's transcript, CuTe (at 1:24:54), is an editorial identification resting on outside knowledge rather than on course material — the lecture's own source never prints it. The transcript header labels it as such.
Lecture 7 is an executable lecture (lecture_07.py), so it is source-text: its figures are recorded by path only and no wiki claim rests on one, exactly as for lectures 1, 2 and 6.

Lecture 7 is the ONE lecture in this KB whose runtime output is quoted rather than withheld, and the reason is that the course publishes it: the program's own stdout from a real four-GPU run is committed to the lectures repo at var/traces/lecture_07_stdout.txt. Its measured collective bandwidths (all-reduce 366-426 GB/s, reduce-scatter 450-490 GB/s on 400 MiB payloads), its per-rank losses and its printed tensors are marked '(recorded run)' and are measurements of THAT machine (Modal, CUDA 13.2, four GPUs, NCCL) - not values a reader's own run will reproduce. The per-rank losses additionally depend on an unseeded random batch. Every bandwidth quoted was independently re-derived from the lecture's own formula and the printed durations, and matches to within one unit in the last place (rounding in the displayed milliseconds).

Lecture 7 cannot be traced the way the other executable lectures can, because it genuinely launches multiple processes. Its spawn() helper detects a tracer and runs the function in a single process with every torch.distributed call replaced by a no-op and rank hard-coded to 0. So the browser trace view shows the code with no communication happening, and any @inspect value that depends on rank shows the rank-0 value only. This is why the separate stdout file exists.

Lecture 7's transcript carries ten [Ed:] notes, several on passages the captions leave genuinely garbled - a 'the first three' that then names four operations, an unparseable 'collective commission' at a paragraph boundary, and a crosstalk fragment at 1:08:54. Where the wiki would otherwise have quoted across one of those gaps it says so instead. One reading, isend/irecv at 1:13:32, rests on outside knowledge of the PyTorch API and is confined to an [Ed:] note; the lecture source never mentions those calls. Adjudication also corrected the drafting agent's own report, which had claimed 'Grace' and 'critical batch size' rested on outside knowledge alone - both words are in fact present in the captions.

lecture_08.pdf prints no page number on any of its 73 pages, so slide citations for lecture 8 are PDF page numbers. The mapping was derived before any page was read and independently confirmed by all five readers over their own ranges; a corner-position text-layer scan returned zero digit tokens across the whole deck.

Lecture 8's deck contradicts itself in one place that matters for citation: slide 70 states Nemotron 3 Super's pipeline-parallel degree as 0 while slide 72's overview table records it as unknown ("??"). Both are transcribed as printed and neither is reconciled.

Lecture 8's deck misspells FSDP as "FDSP" on slides 26, 35 and 63. The slide file transcribes the typo as printed; the transcript and wiki use the correct spelling, since the lecturer says FSDP aloud.

Lecture 8 figure audit: 12 of 73 pages checked across two passes (12, 21, 30, 36, 37, 45, 55, 60, 61, 62, 67, 72). Ten came back clean; four errors were corrected on slides 30 and 37. All 48 cross-slide assertions in the slide file were separately swept, finding three more errors, two of which were in the file's own aggregating front matter rather than in any reader's page.

At 29:53 in the lecture 8 transcript the speaker says "ZeRO stage two" where slide 30 shows he means stage 3. The body records what he said and an [Ed:] note gives the correction, rather than rewriting his words.

Slide 67's Llama 3 failure table has printed percentages summing to 94.9%, not 100%, and they are not percentages of the 419 total interruptions either. The gap is in the source table as pasted; do not compute a percentage from that table's counts.

Slide 44 of lecture 8 prints an eight-category legend of which only five bands are visually separable at any magnification; three categories could not be located and the slide file says so rather than guessing.

Lecture 9's slide deck (lecture_09.pdf, 57 pages) is the most figure-dependent in this KB — 93 pasted images against 2,063 words of native text, about 36 words per page — so its figure descriptions carry the lecture's content rather than illustrating it.

Lecture 9's deck is also the dirtiest transcription in this build. THREE figure-audit passes covered 37 of its 57 pages and found errors on 26 of them, 84 in total, all now corrected. Error classes, in order of how often they recur: SEVEN axes whose scale was unstated or described as linear when logarithmic - by a wide margin the most repeated fault, and the thing to check first on any page of this deck; series endpoints overstated; a colorbar placed on the wrong side; three fabricated or mis-explained source-image defects; three false 'illegible at any magnification' claims that all read cleanly at zoom; and three entries that contradicted themselves, which is the cheapest check available since it needs no PDF at all.

The worst of those, now fixed, had inverted a slide's own argument: misread SuperGlue values on slide 41 led the file to state that the best upstream model falls to mid-pack downstream, when it places about 2nd-3rd of 13. The lecture's actual point is that a mid-table model rises, not that the leader falls.

20 of lecture 9's 57 slide pages have NOT been figure-audited, and page 44 is audited only in part (its panel (a) grid was verified cell by cell; panels (b) and (c) were read at page scale only). Slide TEXT on the unaudited pages is reliable - 56 of 57 headings matched the PDF text layer verbatim and no audited page has shown an error in transcribed prose or a native-text caption - but a CHART VALUE from an unaudited page should be treated as provisional.

Pass 3 finally covered pages 43, 47 and 53, the last of its plan, and all three were dirty - 12 errors, now corrected. Two were undisclosed logarithmic y-axes. Two more were values the wiki had flagged as provisional because they are not spoken aloud and so could not be cross-checked against the transcript: slide 47's Parameters axis in fact runs to 1T rather than 10B, and slide 53's Chinchilla dot sits at about 6.2e23 FLOPs rather than 3-4e23, which agrees with the 5.76e23 Gopher budget the deck itself quotes on slide 47. Those provisional flags can now be removed at the point of use.

Lecture 9's transcript preserves a spoken self-correction: Hashimoto initially reads Kaplan's exponents the wrong way round before correcting himself. Slide 45 settles it as N_opt proportional to C^0.73. The wiki states the corrected form and flags the slip.

wiki/critical-batch-size.md draws on two different lectures and therefore carries timestamps from two different transcripts. The page states explicitly which section cites which, because both lectures discuss the topic around the same point in their runtime.

Images cover lectures 1-10 - the whole of this KB's coverage - but at very different densities, and the difference is not a defect. The five deck lectures have 40-51 images each, one for every figure-bearing page. The five executable lectures have 4-22, because they have no deck: those are the figures the course serves from its own repo, and lecture 10 is much the richest of them at 22. Roughly a third of each deck was deliberately not rendered, so image paths must be READ from a file and never constructed from the pattern.

Images are the only part of this KB that redistributes course material rather than linking to it. The source repository, github.com/stanford-cs336/lectures, carries NO LICENSE file: the material is published for public reading but is not explicitly licensed for redistribution, and the decks reproduce figures from third-party papers (Chinchilla, Wei et al., Kaplan et al., Rosenfeld et al., Shazeer et al., Switch Transformer, OLMoE, DeepSeek, Megatron-LM) plus a screenshot of a public tweet. They are reproduced for study, at the deck's own resolution, with the deck linked at its canonical URL beside every image. AGENTS.md carries the full attribution and the takedown procedure. For lecture 10 the filter was ownership rather than content: all 22 of the course's own images were taken, since a program only calls image() where it wants a figure shown, while the 6 images that lecture hotlinks to third parties (four from the JAX scaling book, one from Baseten, one from Anyscale) were left as URLs. Two of the course's own files were deliberately not fetched: a teaching-staff photo grid, and a four-box diagram whose prose states it completely.

Two rendered images were audited against the PDF as a spot-check of the render pipeline - lecture 9's slide 44 (the Rosenfeld joint-scaling grid, checked cell by cell across all seven rows) and lecture 8's slide 40 (the Megatron tensor-parallel MLP diagram, checked box by box). Both matched raw/slides exactly. This is not a figure audit of the decks; see the per-lecture audit caveats for that.

Lecture 10 is an executable lecture (lecture_10.py, 611 lines), so it is source-text - but it is unlike the other four, because it computes SYMBOLICALLY. FLOPs and bytes are accumulated as sympy expressions in B, S, T, D, F, N, K, H, L and V, simplified, and only then substituted with a Llama 2 13B configuration, so there is nothing machine-dependent to withhold. Every @inspect value in raw/slides/10-inference.md was reproduced by evaluating the lecture's own expression in sympy 1.14 and matches the assert the source makes about it.

Lecture 10's Llama 2 13B latency, throughput and memory figures are THEORETICAL MAXIMA under the source's own stated assumption - 'can overlap compute and communication perfectly and ignore overhead' - not benchmarks. A real serving stack will be slower. They are quoted throughout wiki/latency-and-throughput.md, wiki/kv-cache.md and wiki/attention-variants.md, and every one of them was recomputed here rather than read off the lecture.

Lecture 10's source contradicts its own arithmetic in three places, all recorded as printed in raw/slides/10-inference.md rather than reconciled. (1) The GQA walk-through comments say 'Worse latency, but better throughput' for configurations whose computed latency IMPROVES against the row above; they are consistent only against the B=1 baseline. (2) The TransformerPerformanceStats docstring says num_params is 'in bytes' when it is a count. (3) The quantization section says 'less memory means higher latency/throughput' where it means better. In each case the computed value is the part to trust.

Lecture 10 presents two accuracy claims about GQA that contradict each other, minutes apart, and the KB records both rather than picking. The GQA paper's own evals say quality holds up; DeepSeek-V2's Table 8, shown in the same lecture, puts MHA ahead of GQA on all four hard benchmarks. Percy draws the general moral instead of adjudicating - 'take everything that's not just math with a grain of salt' (51:06). See wiki/attention-variants.md and wiki/multi-head-latent-attention.md.

Lecture 10's 22 images are the course's own PNGs, described by a reader that opened and zoomed each one. Two were independently spot-checked in the parent: mla-accuracy.png (a paper table) was exact cell for cell including the bolding and the verbatim Table 8 caption; gqa-speed.png (a line chart) was structurally right but had stated sub-1 values more precisely than a y-axis with ticks only at 1 and 2 supports, and those were rewritten as relative statements against the reading this KB already audited at higher resolution from lecture 3's slide 63, which shows the same figure. The other 20 descriptions rest on that single reader.

Three details in lecture 10's images are faithful to the source rather than transcription errors: pruning-kd.png prints '9% bettter', paged-attention-sharing.png prints "Je t'amie", and deepseek-v4-attention.png does NOT label the CSA/DSA/HCA acronyms that the lecture's own bullets name immediately after it - it is one general indexer-based sparse-attention diagram.

Lecture 11 is COURSE MATERIAL ONLY. Its deck (lecture_11.pdf, 58 pages) is fully transcribed at raw/slides/11-scaling-laws-in-the-wild.md and 32 of its pages are rendered as images, but there is no transcript of the lecture and no wiki/11-*.md page. A question about lecture 11 can be answered from the deck, with that limit stated; it must not be answered as though the lecture were covered the way lectures 1-10 are.

Lecture 11's slide file has had NO FIGURE AUDIT. Its front matter says so and states the reliability boundary: slide text and tables are reliable, chart values are provisional. That asymmetry is measured, not assumed - every error found in lecture 9's three audit passes was in a chart description and none was in slide text or a native-text caption.

Two values in lecture 11's slide file rest on glyphs of 2-4 pixels and are flagged in its Known limits section rather than presented as read: slide 37's learning-rate axis exponent (read as 1e-3; every LR number on that page scales by 10x if wrong) and slide 11's y-axis tick exponents (read as 1e8/1e9/1e9). Both were attacked with upscaling, ink profiles and cross-correlation against known glyphs before being recorded as uncertain.

Lecture 11's deck is the only one in this KB read at Opus rather than Sonnet. The choice was the user's, put to them because the deck's profile (81 rasters, 1,917 words, 33 words/page - the lowest text density in the build) matched lecture 9, whose Sonnet read produced 84 errors over 26 audited pages. Provenance therefore differs between lecture 11 and lectures 3-9.

Four sentences in lecture 11's deck state a conclusion its own data only partly supports, and the slide file records each rather than repeating the slide: slide 15's 'WSD learning rates work well' holds only for the ~10%-decay variants (the three 2N-decay runs finish worse than the cosine baseline); slides 38 and 40's 'speedup decreases with model size' is not monotone; slide 40's 'matrix-based consistently outperform scalar-based' holds but with the margin collapsing from 0.015 to ~0.005; and slide 43's 'clearly muon works at scale' rests on a panel with no baseline.
